draft.title: Paths and connected networks
card: A path is a route along edges from one vertex to another. It is written as a list of vertices, such as A, B, D.
A network is connected when there is a path between every pair of vertices. If even one vertex cannot be reached from another, the network is not connected.

Roads join towns A and B, B and C, and C and D. You can travel from any town to any other, so the network is connected. Now suppose town E has no road to any other town. Then there is no path from A to E, so the network is not connected.
Paths model real routes. Vertices can be towns, depots or houses, and edges can be roads or delivery routes. A path shows a trip that can be made.
draft.remember: Connected means every vertex can be reached from every other vertex along edges.

a.q: A network has vertices P, Q, R and S. The edges are PQ, QR and PR. Why is the network not connected?
opts: There is no path from S to any other vertex
There is no path from P to Q
The vertices P, Q and R form a closed loop
There are more edges than vertices
a.why: S has no edge, so no path reaches it from P, Q or R. A connected network needs a path between every pair of vertices. The loop PQR does not matter, as P, Q and R are all joined to each other.
a.clue: Check whether every vertex can be reached from every other.

b.q: A courier uses roads between depots. The roads are A to B, B to C, C to D and D to B. Depot E has no road to the others. Which statement is correct?
opts: No path from A to E, so the network is not connected
A to D has a path, so the network is connected
Every depot has a road, so the network is connected
B, C and D form a loop, so the network is not connected
b.why: A path exists from A to D, but none reaches E. A connected network needs a path between every pair, so one unreachable vertex means it is not connected. Having some paths is not enough.
b.clue: One unreachable vertex is enough to break connection.

wants.brief: A network with vertices A, B, C, D joined by edges AB, BC and CD in a line, and a separate vertex E with no edges, labelled as a town with no road.
wants.why: It lets the student see why one unreachable vertex makes a network not connected.

a.best: There is no path from S to any other vertex

b.best: No path from A to E, so the network is not connected
